title: The Double Charge
brief: Linda Park says she paid FixRight Plumbing twice for one water heater repair. The owner says they only charged her once. Read the file, then use the computer to search any company, name, address or number you spot in the documents. Decide: APPROVE her claim or DENY it.

documents.title: Harlow Creek Savings — Dispute reply

body.subject: Your question about two $480 charges
body.body:
We reviewed both transactions. They are NOT a duplicate processing error. They came from two different merchant accounts: FIXRIGHT PLUMBING (10/03) and FXR SERVICES LLC (10/05). Both were keyed in manually with your full card number. If you did not authorize the second one, you may file a fraud claim.

Processor verification for the 10/05/2026 transaction: the authenticated submitting user was Tina Ruiz, billing clerk at FixRight Plumbing. She manually submitted Linda’s stored card details through the FXR SERVICES LLC merchant account. The submission reused FixRight invoice #4471; there was no new repair invoice or additional customer authorization. The original $480 charge settled and was not reversed. The second $480 also settled to FXR SERVICES LLC and was not refunded.

methods.text: The bank processed the same payment twice by mistake.
Linda misread her statement — she was only charged once.
FixRight's billing clerk charged Linda's card a second time through her own company.

solution.explanation: Linda’s claim for the extra $480 is APPROVED. The bank’s processor verification identifies Tina Ruiz as the person who submitted a second settled charge through FXR SERVICES LLC, reusing the paid repair invoice without additional authorization. The registry’s signed ownership filing confirms that Tina owns that company; being a registered agent alone would not prove this. FixRight’s ad independently confirms her billing role, while the bank report rules out Dale’s duplicate-processing theory. Lesson: compare merchant names and verify who actually submitted an unexplained charge.
